description: The wtfalch estate preset. Every repo extends this, so a version the estate shares is decided in one file instead of twenty. Extend it with "extends": ["github>wtfalch/ci-templates"].

minimumReleaseAge holds a version for three days before Renovate will propose it. The npm supply-chain compromises that mattered were caught and unpublished within hours, so a short hold turns most of them into a release we simply never saw.

internalChecksFilter: strict is the other half. Without it Renovate falls back to a version that has not aged yet when nothing else satisfies the range, which is exactly the situation an attacker creates.

@wtfalch packages are exempt from the hold: they publish from release.yml over OIDC with no stored token, so there is no credential to steal, and an estate bump that waits three days is a bump that arrives after the consumer needed it.

packageRules.description: Group all non-major npm updates into a single weekly PR

THE POSTGRES MAJOR THE ESTATE RUNS. This is the source of truth: raise the ceiling here and every repo gets a pull request moving it up, lower it and nothing is proposed. The tag is hardcoded two or three times per repo -- a CI service container, a compose file, a string inside a script -- so no repo is the place to decide it. 17 is where auth, jobs, keys, raincheck, raincheck-dos, lokessmie-app and package-template already are; the remaining repos are on 16 and will each get one pull request.

Estate packages get their own pull request, never grouped. They are pinned exactly on purpose, a minor can change behaviour inside a 0.x, and a bump that arrives inside a ten-package group is a bump nobody read. This rule is LAST because Renovate lets a later rule override an earlier one, and the npm grouping rule above would otherwise pull these back in.

customManagers.description: Postgres image tags written as string literals in TypeScript and scripts. No manager parses those, so without this the Coolify bootstrap step and every docker-run helper drift away from the CI pin silently.
